Its unique simple eigenvalue below the continuum is mu-s_* with mu F_b(s_*)=1, because F_b is strictly decreasing and diverges at zero. The eigenvector (s_*+lambda)^-1 has squared projection B=1/(mu^2 M2)=b s_*/(mu(mu-s_*)). Cox-age survival equals the Feynman–Kac expectation; its spectral measure provides a positive Gaussian heat-kernel mixture. The continuous spectral support gives the explicit exponential error bound using the first spectral moment b. Stieltjes inversion recovers the continuum density. Exponential-integral asymptotics prove the rare-refresh essential singularity and distinguish strict tail from variance. The packaged verifier numerically compares the spectral inversion and the independent renewal transform; computations are checks, not the proof.

value.rationale: Far-tail decay rates are central measurable localization properties for fluctuating-reset diffusion. The existing paper links a small-frequency estimate to the far-tail localization scale; the theorem proves their asymptotic inequivalence, supplies the exact corrected exponent and coefficient with a uniform exponentially faster remainder, and identifies an exponentially faint spectral mode. The square-decay-rate discrepancy diverges in the physically natural slow-refresh limit; this resolves a substantive distinction between moment-based and extreme-event observables.
